sentences.text: Heard on I.A. No. 2607/2025 an application for condonation of delay of 23 days in filing this appeal.
For the reasons mentioned in the application, the same is allowed and the delay in filing this appeal is hereby condoned.
Heard on the question of admission.

This appeal under Section 71 (6) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been filed against the order dated 8.1.2025 passed by 9th District Judge, Gwalior in RCA. No. 360/2024 as well as order dated 25.10.2024 passed by the Adjudicating Officer in Case No. Q/Food Safety/08/2023 by which appellant was punished for committing breach of Section 26 (2) (v) and Section 27 (3) (a) as well as under Section 58 of Food Safety Act.

It is not out of place to mention here that Adjudicating Officer had imposed penalty of fine of Rs. 2,00,000/- whereas the appellate authority has reduced it to Rs.
1,00,000/-.
According to the prosecution case, the appellant is alleged to have used Nestle Chocolate (Kit Kat) which had already expired.

Although, it is submitted by counsel for appellant that no undue advantage was gained by the Manoj Singh Mawai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186207197/
1 appellant by using the expired chocolate but the same cannot be a ground for acquittal.

entities.text: Manoj Singh Mawai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant was aware of the fact that shelf life of the chocolate in question has already expired and in spite of that he was using it for preparing shake.
This Court is of the considered opinion that no case is made out for warranting interference in this appeal.
Even otherwise, this Court is of the view that the appellate Court has already shown undue sympathetic view towards the appellant.
Accordingly, orders dated 08.01.2025 and 25.10.2024 are hereby affirmed.
Appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
